The proposal's 'factor exactly 1.00', '50.50/1.01 = 50.00' and 3.06% 'total-return series' are wrong.

verdicts.reason: Original correct. The code reproduces 2.93/0.19. A 500-history simulation gives 60-parameter 3.08 IS / 0.01 OOS and 1-parameter 0.38 / 0.00, matching the lesson. The 'always long or short' rule's sign is fitted in-sample, so it IS a 1-parameter rule; 'no fitted parameter' is wrong. Returns are zero-mean by construction, so 'Neither rule could ever earn' is true. The 'digits depend on library version' paragraph is false hedging (the numpy Generator stream is fixed).

verdicts.title: The Kelly criterion: the bet size that grows money fastest
verdicts.reason: Mostly wrong. The expected gain per round as a fraction of the account is f × 0.2 = 2%, 4%, 8%, so '0.2 × 0.4 = 0.08' and '+8%' are right and '+3.2%' is wrong. Zero log growth is at f = 0.389 = 1.95 × Kelly, so 'about twice Kelly' is right and '1.67 times' is wrong. 'Lose money' fits the 0.78 factor. Only the clearer sentence 'One win at 1.4 does not recover a loss at 0.6' (1.4 × 0.6 = 0.84) is accepted.

edits.old: One loss at 0.6 undoes more than one win at 1.4 gives back.
edits.new: One win at 1.4 does not recover a loss at 0.6.
